passage: I'm Sunaina. At the back of my rough notebook, on the last page, I wrote Vikas's name in tiny letters and then covered it with a doodle of a flower. My heart thumped whenever the notebook slid out of my bag. I did not want anyone teasing me. Only my best friend Rani knew, because I had decided she was kind and never repeated things. I told her at the water tank, whispering, and she just squeezed my hand and said, "Your secret is safe." Now, when Vikas laughs in class, I feel a warm tickle inside, and nobody else needs to know about it.

qa.q: Where did Sunaina write Vikas's name?
qa.a: Sunaina wrote it in tiny letters on the last page of the rough notebook.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel about anyone seeing Vikas's name?
qa.a: Sunaina felt nervous and afraid of being teased, with a thumping heart whenever the notebook slid out, so the name went under a flower doodle.

qa.q: How did Sunaina choose who to tell?
qa.a: Sunaina picked a best friend, Rani, because Rani is kind and never repeats things.

qa.q: How might Rani feel about being trusted with the secret?
qa.a: Rani probably felt trusted and caring, since she squeezed Sunaina's hand and promised the secret was safe. 😊

grounding: A child keeps a first crush private and shares it only with one kind friend.

passage:
In her maths notebook, on the very last page, Lucia wrote Paulo's name in tiny letters. Then she drew a sun over it so nobody could read it.
Every time the notebook slid out of her bag at school in Lisbon, her heart pounded. What if someone saw?
It was her feeling, and she liked keeping it private. But one day she wanted to tell someone.
She thought about who. Not Marta, who told everyone everything. She chose Inês, who had once kept her secret about the lost library book.
"Promise you won't tell?"
Inês smiled. "Promise. It's nice, Lucia."
Lucia felt lighter.

How did Lucia feel whenever the notebook slid out of her bag?
qa.a: She felt nervous, with her heart pounding, afraid someone would see the name.

qa.q: Why was Inês a good choice to tell?
qa.a: Inês had kept a secret before, unlike Marta, who told everyone everything.

qa.q: How might Inês feel about being trusted?
qa.a: Inês seems pleased and kind, promising to keep it and saying it's nice.

grounding: A girl writes a boy's name secretly in her notebook, keeps the feeling private, and chooses a kind friend who will not spread it when she tells.

passage:
In the hostel study room, Tanu opened her diary to the last page. There, in the corner, she had written "Lokesh" and circled it lightly. She quickly flipped the page when footsteps passed.
Lokesh was in her science group. She liked the way he explained things slowly. It was a warm, private feeling, and she wanted to keep it that way.
But at night she sometimes wanted to talk about it. She thought about Sahil, her friend since Class 3, who never gossiped.
Next day by the water cooler, she whispered, "Can I tell you something private?"
Sahil listened, nodded, and said, "Safe with me." He never mentioned it to anyone.

qa.q: Where did Tanu write Lokesh's name?
qa.a: On the last page of her diary, in the corner.

qa.q: How did Tanu feel about her crush?
qa.a: She felt it was a warm, private feeling she wanted to protect, and she was nervous when footsteps passed.

qa.q: Why was Sahil a good person to tell?
qa.a: He had been her friend since Class 3 and never gossiped, and he kept it to himself.

qa.q: How might Sahil feel being trusted with Tanu's secret?
qa.a: Sahil may feel trusted and respectful, simply keeping it safe.

grounding: A girl secretly writes a boy's name in her diary, keeps the feeling private, and tells only a kind friend who will not spread it.
